import pytest
import click
from click.testing import CliRunner

def test_runner_catch_exceptions_default():
    @click.command()
    def cli_error():
        raise ValueError("This is an error")

    runner = CliRunner()
    # The default for catch_exceptions is True, so the exception should be caught
    result = runner.invoke(cli_error)
    assert result.exception is not None
    assert isinstance(result.exception, ValueError)
    assert result.exit_code == 1

    # Now, if we set catch_exceptions to False on the runner, it should propagate
    # This is the behavior the user expects to be able to configure globally
    runner.catch_exceptions = False
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="This is an error"):
        runner.invoke(cli_error)

    # Test that passing it directly to invoke still overrides the runner's setting
    runner.catch_exceptions = False
    result = runner.invoke(cli_error, catch_exceptions=True)
    assert result.exception is not None
    assert isinstance(result.exception, ValueError)
    assert result.exit_code == 1
